title: The Burnt Deadline
premise: Sebastian Eriksen, a financial-crimes investigator haunted by a raid that went wrong, receives a calendar invite from his handler, Ingrid Voss — sent hours after her death. The meeting pulls him into a conspiracy to launder a cartel's fortune through the very regulatory system he serves, and the 'secret worth killing for' is a ledger key hidden in his own fragmented memory of the incident he can't remember. Hunted by both the cartel and corrupt colleagues inside his agency, Sebastian must decide whether justice means exposing everyone or protecting the one person he loves: Mara, the cartel's reluctant accountant and his only witness. In the end, Sebastian trades the ledger key for Mara's life, burns the evidence publicly at the cost of his career, and finally sleeps through the night.
about_author: Mirabel Villalobos is a former compliance analyst who spent a decade tracing money through shell companies before turning to fiction full-time. She writes thrillers from a small coastal town where she claims the fog helps her plot.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Insomniac Sebastian reviews clean-money cases by night until an email arrives from Ingrid Voss — timestamped after her reported death, inviting him to a meeting tomorrow at 9 a.m. He verifies her death certificate himself. The beat is dread sharpening into compulsion: he RSVPs yes.

chapters.title: Clean Hands
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Flashback-tinged morning routine establishes the incident eighteen months ago: a raid, gunfire, a gap in his memory. His supervisor, Deputy Director Hale, presses him about the Voss email before Sebastian mentions it. Emotional beat: paranoia — who already knows?

chapters.title: Nine O'Clock
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. At the meeting site — a shuttered marina office — Sebastian finds no Ingrid, only a dead drop: a burner phone, a partial ledger printout, and a note in her handwriting: 'You already have the rest.' A black SUV arrives; he flees. Beat: terror fused with purpose.

chapters.title: The Accountant
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Introduce Mara Quintero, forensic accountant coerced into servicing the Serrano cartel's laundering network, who recognizes the ledger fragment as her own work. She realizes someone is reconstructing it — and that reconstruction will kill her. Beat: cornered intelligence.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The burner phone rings: a voice claiming to be Ingrid's dead handler network tells him the ledger key is encoded in his missing memory of the raid. Hale summons him for a psych evaluation — clearly a loyalty test. Beat: the past becomes the weapon.

chapters.title: Two Ledgers
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara discovers the cartel runs two books — one for regulators, one real — and that Ingrid Voss had been her secret contact for months. She finds Voss's last message addressed to 'the man who forgot.' Beat: grief and resolve entwined.

chapters.title: Collision
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Sebastian traces the ledger fragment to a shell company; Mara is sent to audit the same company. They meet in a conference room, each recognizing the other as either salvation or threat. Beat: electric mutual suspicion tipping toward alliance.

chapters.title: What the Raid Buried
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Under hypnosis-adjacent recall triggered by the marina, Sebastian remembers fragments: Ingrid alive during the raid, handing him something, a colleague's gun. He realizes the 'incident' was staged to bury the ledger in his head. Beat: betrayal of everything he served.

chapters.title: Tail Lights
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The cartel notices Mara's off-book queries. Her handler, Tomás, gives her one chance to prove loyalty: identify the investigator poking the shells. She lies — badly. Beat: love against duty begins its first real cost.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Sebastian and Mara meet off-grid; she confirms the ledger structure, he supplies the agency-side names. They compute what exposure means: both dead within days unless they control the release. Beat: intimacy forged under countdown pressure.

chapters.title: Hale's Ledger
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian confronts Hale with circumstantial proof of agency complicity; Hale offers promotion and amnesia in exchange for the recovered fragment. Sebastian records the conversation — then finds his recorder wiped remotely. Beat: the enemy is inside the walls.

chapters.title: Ingrid's Voice
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The burner delivers a scheduled message: Ingrid recorded it before dying, explaining she hid the key in Sebastian because trauma made him the safest vault — and naming her killer's initial: H. Beat: mourning weaponized into mission.

chapters.title: The Serrano Summons
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Cartel patriarch Emilio Serrano summons Mara, having learned of her contact with Voss. He offers her a devil's trade: deliver the investigator and the key, and her family lives. Beat: duty crushing love from the other direction.

chapters.title: Trade Drafts
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Sebastian and Mara draft competing plans: he wants to go public via a journalist; she insists the cartel will kill the journalist and them both before print. First real fight. Beat: love tested by incompatible ethics.

chapters.title: Night Swim
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Ambushed at his apartment, Sebastian escapes through the marina — the same water from the raid triggers near-total recall: Hale ordered the raid, Ingrid died passing him the drive, and Sebastian himself fired back. Beat: guilt reframed as survival.

chapters.title: Confession at Dawn
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara confesses the Serrano ultimatum to Sebastian. Instead of rage, he proposes using it: let the cartel 'capture' him, walk him to the real ledger, and burn it from inside. Beat: trust as the ultimate gamble.

chapters.title: The Handover
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The staged capture goes wrong when Hale's men shadow the cartel team — three factions converge on one warehouse. Mara is taken; Sebastian escapes with a partial key. Beat: plan collapse, stakes maximized.

chapters.title: Interrogation Light
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Held in the warehouse, Mara stalls Serrano by feeding him doctored ledger math while secretly noting exits and guard rotations. Hale's mole inside the cartel reveals himself. Beat: wit as resistance.

chapters.title: Deadline
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. With journalist ally Priya Nair holding the partial evidence, Sebastian walks into the warehouse offering the full key — his memory — in exchange for Mara. Serrano accepts; Hale's team breaches early. Beat: the trade made at gunpoint.

chapters.title: Fire Sale
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Chaos: fire, gunfire, Sebastian reciting the key aloud to buy seconds, Mara turning the guards' own accounting against them. Hale arrives to silence everyone; Ingrid's posthumous dead-man switch releases files to every regulator simultaneously. Beat: climax — truth as detonation.

chapters.title: Aftermath Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Hale arrested; Serrano escaped but financially gutted; Sebastian suspended pending inquiry, testimony given freely this time. He and Mara reckon with what the trade cost — his memory now voluntarily surrendered, not stolen. Beat: exhausted honesty.

chapters.title: First Sleep
chapters.summary: Dual POV epilogue. Weeks later, on the coast, Sebastian sleeps through the night beside Mara; the final image is the sunrise over the marina, unhaunted. A postcard arrives unsigned: 'Some ledgers stay open.' Beat: peace earned, vigilance retained.
